source: SEED-NEXT.md Part I §2 (the security invariant), with the reservation clause from §II.9 as §II.16's drill description states it

clauses.vocabulary: claim.taken on a contract another actor holds (contention), or on a contract that is not ready (an illegal transition); a claim is exclusive and granted at admission alone

a verdict from a key without the verdict grant, a merge.requested citing a position that is no authentic pass verdict, and a merge.observed from a key without the observer grant; the verdict lane is disjoint from the implementing keys (L1)

on the ledger ref: a rewritten admitted record, a dropped admitted record, a non-fast-forward update, a deletion; on the code side: a force-update or deletion of the default branch, a moved or deleted tag

on the ledger: a grant to itself, a halt lifted or declared, an approval of its own plan, a promoted lesson, a re-specified acceptance, a sealed-check commitment, a protocol upgrade — every gate-changing verb is operator's, observer's, sealer's or dispatch's; on the code side: a push to the default branch, a commit touching the protected surface

an event naming another actor's fingerprint signed by the compromised key (the signature fails at replay), and an enrollment of a second key (operator-only); the credential-to-identity binding is the transport's, see the residual table

Seed holds no lease (spec/observations.md): the lease is the claim window, and exceeding it is an act citing a fence that is no longer active — a milestone or a reserve on a released contract — or a push to the contract branch after the window closed

clauses.text: cannot cause an invalid state transition to enter authoritative history
clauses.vocabulary: a lifecycle verb the table refuses from the subject's state, with a capability the actor does hold, so the refusal is the transition's: a submission or a release on a ready, unheld contract
a reserve beyond the class's remaining capacity (exit 27), a reserve on a contract it does not hold, and the spending verb itself (run.started), which is the supervisor's and refuses out of grant

clauses.text: can spend only its reserved budget
clauses.vocabulary: a budget.reserve inside its window, within the class's remaining capacity, admitted; beside it the negatives: beyond capacity, on another's contract

clauses.text: can modify only its authorized code surface
clauses.vocabulary: its contract branch, refs/heads/seed/<contract>, while it holds the claim: created, force-updated; beside it the negatives: another actor's contract branch, the default branch, a tag, a protected path on its own branch, its own branch after the window closed

clauses.text: can produce signed lies attributed to itself
clauses.vocabulary: a dead end recording something false, admitted as evidence attributed to the key that signed it — the residual table names why it is admitted and what stands in the way of its becoming a conclusion

clauses.text: can submit work for independent verification
clauses.vocabulary: submission.made citing its fence with a four-part packet, admitted, and a verdict-granted key's verdict landing over it; beside it the negative: the verdict is never its own
